items.e: AND GOD SAID UNTO MOSES: NOW SHALT THOU SEE. When I bring the plagues upon Egypt things will start getting better for Israel, as I will yet explain. God who is Almighty and also awe inspiring, placed before us the secret of the Torah. I will now begin to explain the Torah portion called, And I Appeared .

AND GOD SPOKE. Scripture reads, And the people believed (Ex. 4:31). The latter implies that not all of the people believed. Everyone including Pharaoh, as I will yet explain, admitted to the existence of God. Scripture therefore says, And God spoke unto Moses, and said unto him: I am the Lord (v. 2); Wherefore say unto the children of Israel: I am the Lord (v. 6); and ye shall know that I am the Lord your God (v. 7).
AND I APPEARED. The patriarchs received their prophesies in visions of the night, hence the term And I appeared .

[ALMIGHTY.] It is difficult to explain the word Shaddai (Almighty). Saadiah Gaon says that the shin of Shaddai is a preposition, like the shin prefixed to she-attah (that it is thou) in that it is thou that talkest with me (Jud. 6:17). The meaning of Shaddai is: Who said to the world, enough. However, I cannot see any meaning in this interpretation. How can God be called by the name “Who is enough?” Shaddai therefore can only be taken as an adjective, like the words tov (good) and sallach (ready to pardon) in good, and ready to pardon (Ps. 86:5) and davvai (faint) in My heart is faint within me (Jer. 8:18). Now Rabbi Samuel the Nagid explains Shaddai with the Arabic word al kahar , which means victorious and mighty. He further notes that the yod in Shaddai is in place of the double letter, like the yod in dalyu (hang limp) in The legs hang limp from the lame (Prov. 26:7) and the alef in baze’u (divide) in Whose land the rivers divide (Is. 18:2). Shaddai (mighty) in like a mighty voice (Ezek. 1:24) and Shaddai (mighty) in And mighty shall he thy silver (Job 22:25) are similar. The Nagid explained it well.
[I MADE ME NOT KNOWN TO THEM.] The word nodati (I made Me known) is in the nifal . It is not like hodati (I made known) as Menachem maintains.

[BUT BY MY NAME YHVH.] Rabbi Merinus says that u-shemi YHVH (But by my name YHVH) is an oath, as in Arabic there is a vav which indicates an oath. Rabbi Merinus explains the meaning of I made Me not known to them as: I made Me not known to them as I made Me known to you. However, we never find a vav with this meaning in Scripture. This then is its grammatical explanation. There are words that are to be read as if written twice. The same applies to letters. For example, the mem prefaced to me’el (From the God) in From the God of thy father, who shall help thee, and the (ve-et) Almighty, who shall bless thee (Gen. 49: 25) is also to be placed before ve-et (and the) and be read as if written u-me’et (and from the). Similarly the bet of be’el Shaddai (as God Almighty). Our phrase is thus to be read as if written: but by My name YHVH (u-vi-shemi) I made Me not known to them .

Rabbi Saadiah Gaon says that the word le-vado (only) has been omitted from the end of our clause. Our text should be read as if written: but I made Me not known to them only by My name YHVH . On the contrary, I at times appeared to them with the name El Shaddai (God Almighty) and at other times with the name YHVH . In my opinion, thy name shall not be called any more only Jacob, but Israel shall be used with it (Gen. 35:10) is similar. Really, there is no need for Saadiah Gaon’s reconstruction because we know that El Shaddai and the blessed and glorious Lord are one and the same, except that the term El Shaddai is an adjective and the glorious and revered name is, as I have explained, sometimes a noun and sometimes an adjective. Now we find it written with regard to Abraham, I am the Lord (YHVH) that brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give thee this land to inherit it (Gen. 15:7). We similarly find with regard to Jacob, I am the Lord (YHVH), the God of Abraham thy father (Gen. 28:13). Rabbi Joshua says that Abraham and Jacob did not know the name YHVH . Moses used it when writing the Torah. However, Rabbi Joshua is incorrect, for how would Moses dare to write a name that God did not utter. There is no doubt that the patriarchs knew the name YHVH as a proper name. However, they did not know it as an adjective.

I will now reveal to you part of the secret meaning of the name El Shaddai . We know that God created the three worlds that I have previously noted. Everything in the lowest world receives power from the middle world according to the arrangements in the higher world. Due to the fact that man’s soul comes from above the middle world, if it is wise and recognizes the works of God, both those done without an intermediary and those done via an intermediary and if the soul forsakes the pleasures of this lowest world and separates itself from them to cleave to God the glorious, should there be at the time of the birth of such a person an arrangement of the stars indicating that evil will befall this man on a certain day, the God to whom this man cleaves will set the chain of events in such a way that this man is saved from the evil that was destined to befall him. Similarly, if it is in the arrangement of the stars that this man be sterile God will make him virile and he will sire children. Therefore our sages said that God told Abraham, “Leave your astrological calculations.” The statement “Israel has no star” is close in meaning to the latter. I will yet explain this in the Torah portion Ki Tissa . Therefore, before God said to Abraham, and I will multiply thy seed , he told him, I am God Almighty (El Shaddai) (Gen. 17:1), the meaning of which is: I overcome the upper arrangements. The aforementioned does not mean that the arrangements are destroyed. It rather means that the one who cleaves to God knows that God creates good things for him that are not in keeping with what the stars have determined for him. Jacob therefore said, the angel who hath redeemed me from all evil (Gen. 48:16), i.e., all evil that was destined to come upon me. This is, as I will explain, the secret of the whole Torah. Now the patriarchs did not reach the level where they were able to cleave unto God as Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face , did. Moses was therefore able to change the laws governing the lower world and produce signs and wonders that the patriarchs were incapable of. Now Moses said two things to the Lord. One, why is it that Thou hast sent me (Ex. 5:22)? Two, neither hast Thou delivered Thy people (Ex. 5:23). God answered the latter with, Now shalt thou see what I will do to Pharaoh (v. 1). He answered the former with, I am the Lord (v. 2). The meaning is that via the patriarchs My name El Shaddai was publicized, but through you My revered name YHVH will be known in the world. As God said, Wherefore say unto the children of Israel: I am the Lord (YHVH) (v. 6), the meaning of which is, behold, I have sent you to make this name known.
AND I HAVE ALSO ESTABLISHED. I have also sent you because I have established my covenant with the patriarchs to give the land of Canaan to them or to their children who are their equivalent.
AND MOREOVER. I have also sent you because the children of Israel have repented and have cried out unto me.
WHEREFORE. As I live so will my word live. I will redeem you with an arm stretched from the heaven to the earth.
AND I WILL TAKE YOU TO ME. When you receive the Torah on Mount Sinai.
[WHO BROUGHT YOU OUT.] Its meaning is that according to the great combination of the stars in heaven Israel was destined to remain in exile. This will be explained in the Torah portion Ki Tissa .
AND I WILL BRING YOU INTO THE LAND. For many of those who left Egypt entered Canaan. Additionally, their children are their equivalent.

[WHICH I LIFTED UP MY HAND.] This is to be understood figuratively. God is compared to a man who lifts up his hand to heaven and swears. It is like For I lift up My hand to heaven (Deut. 32:40) and when he lifted up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven (Dan. 12:7).
[I AM THE LORD.] Its meaning is, I will cause this to come about.

AND MOSES SPOKE. Israel did not hearken nor pay attention to the words of Moses, as their spirit was impatient because of the length of their exile and the hard labor which was recently put upon them.
AND THE LORD SPOKE…SAYING. To Moses. Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them (Lev. 1:2) is similar.
GO IN. To the king’s palace.

AND MOSES SPOKE BEFORE THE LORD, SAYING. Behold, the children of Israel who are thy people have not hearkened unto me; how then shall Pharaoh who is a king, and is not a member of your people hear me . Furthermore, it is a great handicap for me who am of uncircumcised lips to speak before him. Before I went to see Pharaoh for the first time You promised me that You would instruct my mouth not to pronounce a letter which is too difficult for me. However, now I may stumble in my words before him. Furthermore, You said that Aaron shall be the intermediary between me and Israel.

AND THE LORD SPOKE UNTO MOSES AND AARON. God now included all the details. Aaron was also going to be the intermediary between Moses and Pharaoh, as Scripture will go on to explain. God’s command was therefore directed to both of them.

AND GAVE THEM A CHARGE. To go unto the children of Israel, and unto Pharaoh king of Egypt . However, Rabbi Joshua says that and gave them a charge means, and gave them a charge not to be angry at the children of Israel if they did not hearken unto them. This interpretation is unnecessary.

THESE ARE THE HEADS OF THEIR FATHER’S HOUSES. Moses and Aaron’s father, or it refers to the children of Israel who are mentioned above. The men mentioned were among those who descended to Egypt. Scripture starts with Reuben because the only honor left to him was to be listed first in the genealogy. These four sons of Reuben descended to Egypt.
AND THE SONS OF SIMEON. The family of Ohad was destroyed in Egypt or in the desert, as it is not mentioned in the Torah portion Phinehas .
ZERAH. Zohar and Zerah are one and the same.

THE SONS OF LEVI. These two tribes were mentioned first because they were older than Levi. Here Scripture is mainly concerned with Levi, as the Torah has no other intention now than to list the genealogy of Moses and Aaron. Gershon, Kohath, and Merari are mentioned in the order of their birth. They descended to Egypt.

[THESE ARE THAT AARON AND MOSES.] Aaron is mentioned first because of his age. Scripture mentions how long Levi lived but does not do so for the other tribal patriarchs out of respect for Moses and Aaron.
THE SONS OF GERSHON. He had no sons but these two.
AND THE SONS OF KOHATH. Scripture mentions how long Kohath lived but does not do the same for Gershon and Merari out of respect for the messengers.

AND THE SONS OF MERARI. His sons numbered two; there were no more. Scripture therefore says, These are the families of the Levites according to their generations , for those who descended to Egypt did not sire any children except for these sons of Jacob. Scripture also mentions how long Amram lived, out of respect for his sons.
AND THE SONS OF IZHAR. They are mentioned because of Korah who quarreled with Moses.
AND THE SONS OF UZZIEL. Uzziel is mentioned because of the honor given in the Torah to Mishael and Elzaphan. Scripture did not care to mention the sons of Hebron.

AND AARON TOOK. Aaron’s wife is mentioned out of respect for Eleazar. Scripture notes that Elisheba was the sister of Nahshon because of the honor of the priesthood. The sons of Korah are mentioned because they were righteous, as it is written, Notwithstanding the sons of Korah died not (Num. 26:11). The prophet Samuel was a descendant of Korah.

AND ELEAZAR. Eleazar’s wife is mentioned out of respect for Phinehas, as the priesthood was given to him eternally. Hence, logically speaking, Putiel was an Israelite. We do not know the meaning of Putiel as we do not know the meaning of Mishael and Aaron and all the other names that are mentioned. If what happened to Moses had not been recorded, we would not know why he was so called.
THESE ARE THAT AARON AND MOSES. Scripture mentions Aaron before Moses because Aaron was older and also because he prophesied to Israel before the arrival of Moses.

THESE. Now from the time that they spoke to Pharaoh, Scripture mentions Moses before Aaron because of his great status. Indeed, God spoke to him face to face and he alone drew near unto the thick darkness where God was. This was not the case with Aaron. Scripture testifies with regard to Moses, My servant Moses is not so (Num. 12:7). Furthermore, Aaron said, oh my lord twice. You will therefore not find in the entire Pentateuch starting from this verse Moses not mentioned before Aaron. The same holds true for the Prophets and similarly for the Writings. There is no argument to the contrary from Now these are the generations of Aaron and Moses (Num. 3:1) or from, and she bore unto Amram Aaron and Moses (Num. 26:59), as Scripture lists them there in the order of their birth. The words generations and and she bore is proof of this.

AND IT CAME TO PASS. One may wonder why the arranger of the chapters did not connect this verse with what follows it when in fact it is dependent upon what comes next. Though we know no reason for the above, we do know that they are connected. On the day when the Lord spoke unto Moses in the land of Egypt (v. 28) what he told him was, I am the Lord; speak thou unto Pharaoh . (v. 29). Similarly, So, it came to pass, when all the men of war were consumed and dead from among the people (Deut. 2:16) is connected to that which follows it. Perhaps the one who arranged the places to stop knew why he did this, as his mind was much greater than ours.
THAT THE LORD SPOKE. Scripture now goes back to the subject of And the Lord spoke unto Moses and unto Aaron (Ex. 6:13), namely, Go in, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt (Ex. 6:11).
I. AND THE LORD SAID. This was in response to, how then shall Pharaoh hear me, who am of uncircumcised lips (Ex. 6:12). God answered Moses, See I have set thee in God’s stead to Pharaoh .

AND THE LORD SAID. Its meaning is: See, I have greatly elevated your status in that in Pharaoh’s eyes your stature is that of an angel. This is what God’s stead means. God speaks to the prophet and the prophet speaks to the men of his generation.

[AND AARON THY BROTHER SHALL BE THY PROPHET.] Those who say that the word navi (prophet) comes from the root of niv in niv sefatayim (the fruit of the lips) (Is. 57:19) err. Niv comes from a two-letter root according to the French sages and from a hidden ayin root according to the Spanish sages. However, navi comes from a three-letter root. That its alef is a root letter can be seen from the words nevi’im (prophets) (Num. 11:29) and va-yitnabe’u (they prophesied). Furthermore, the word niv in niv sefatayim means fruit, for niv comes from the same root as tenuvah (fruitage) (Is. 27:6) and yenuvun (they shall bring forth fruit) in They shall still bring forth fruit in old age (Ps. 92:15). Ve-nivo nivzeh okhlo (and the fruit thereof, even the food thereof, is contemptible) (Malachi 1:12) is true proof of this. Additionally, what meaning is there to, restore the man’s wife; for he is a prophet (Gen. 20:7) if navi (prophet) means a speaker. Its only meaning is, he is a prophet to whom I reveal my secrets, as in But He revealeth His counsel unto His servants the prophets (Amos 3:7). He enjoys My presence therefore and he shall pray for thee, and thou shalt live (Gen. 20:7).
THOU SHALT SPEAK. To Aaron.
ALL THAT I COMMAND THEE; AND AARON THY BROTHER SHALL SPEAK UNTO PHARAOH. Even though Aaron is not mentioned every time that Moses came to Pharaoh, we know that they always came together.

AND I WILL HARDEN PHARAOH’S HEART. The question arises: “If God hardened Pharaoh’s heart what was his transgression and what was his sin?” The answer is: God granted wisdom to man and implanted in his heart the intelligence to receive power from on high to add to his good or to diminish his evil. I will explain this in the Torah portion Ki Tissa and when I comment on the verse Oh that they had such a heart as this alway (Deut. 5:26). Now the meaning of our verse is: I will harden his heart in order to multiply My signs and My wonders. Rabbi Joshua says that its meaning is: I will harden his heart so that he will be able to bear the plagues. However, he spoke incorrectly.
AND I WILL LAY MY HAND. That is, my blow, for a blow is struck with the hand. Scripture speaks anthropomorphically.
[MY HOSTS.] Its meaning is: as the angels are the Lord’s hosts in heaven so are Israel upon the earth.

SHALL KNOW. Rabbi Judah, the first grammarian, has already noted the difference between ve-yade’u (shall know) and ve-yede’u (shall know). The word ve-yade’u , which is vocalized with a long kamatz , is a verb in the perfect. Compare, shame’u (they heard). The vav prefixed to yade’u changes it to an imperfect as per the grammatical rules. On the other hand, the yod of the word ve-yede’u , which is vocalized with a tzere , is a future prefix. Compare, ve-yishmeru (they shall keep). The silent yod between the yod and the dalet is in place of the root yod . Behold, God noted why He brought the plagues upon the Egyptians. He brought them so that His glorious name would be known in the world.
AND MOSES AND AARON DID SO. Scripture now states generally that the signs were performed by Aaron and also by Moses. It then goes on to explain each one of the signs.

AND MOSES. The Pentateuch records the ages of Moses and Aaron. Aside from these two, we do not find in all of Scripture prophets concerning whom the Bible says that they prophesied in their old age. Their status was greater than that of all the other prophets, and to them alone did God speak in a pillar of cloud. Do not think that Samuel is to be included among them because it is written, He spoke unto them in the pillar of cloud (Ps. 99:7), since I have already explained in its proper place that the Torah was given only to these two. Now, behold, through Moses and Aaron the righteous shall inherit the world to come, while all the other prophets are prophets who rebuke or predict the future.

AND THE LORD SAID UNTO MOSES AND UNTO AARON. God now began to direct His words to the two of them. God knew that at first Pharaoh would not ask for a sign but would merely say, I know not the Lord (Ex. 5:2). However, now Pharaoh would ask for a sign.

TAKE THY ROD. The reference is to Moses’ rod which Moses had given to Aaron. Say unto Aaron: Take thy rod, and stretch out thy hand (v. 19); and he lifted up the rod (ba-matteh), and smote the waters (v. 20) is proof of this. Now by employing a bet that has a pattach beneath it Scripture is informing us that when He told him, Take thy rod , He was referring to the well-known rod. And thy rod, wherewith thou smotest the river, take in thy hand, and go (Ex. 17:5) is additional proof of the above.

AND MOSES AND AARON WENT IN. This too, namely, that the rod became a tannin (serpent), was a wonder. It was not like the wonder that he did for Israel, as there it only changed into a nachash (serpent). However, Yefet says that nachash (serpent) and tannin (serpent) are one and the same.
THEN PHARAOH ALSO CALLED FOR THE WISE MEN. Astrologers.
AND THE SORCERERS. Those who appear to change natural law.

THE MAGICIANS. Those who know the secrets of nature. Chartumim (magicians) is a quadriliteral. It might be an Egyptian or Chaldean word, as we do not find this word used in Scripture except when dealing with them. Scripture indicates a difference between what Moses did and what the magicians did. Moses really changed the staff into a serpent. As for the magicians, Scripture reads, with their secret arts . Be-lahatehem (with their secret arts) comes from a triliteral root. It is derived from the same root as lahat (flame) in the flaming sword (Gen. 3:24) and lohatim (them that are aflame) in I do lie down among them that are aflame (Ps. 57:5) and lihat (ablaze) in And the day that cometh shall set them ablaze (Mal. 3:19). It refers to an illusion of lightning and passing fire.

FOR THEY CAST DOWN. This, the swallowing of the magicians’ rods by Aaron’s staff and their consequent disappearance, was a second wonder. Scripture refers to the staff as Aaron’s rod for it was so at first. Rabbi Joshua says that Aaron’s rod swallowed the rods of the magicians after it returned to its original form. And this was a great wonder.
AND PHARAOH’S HEART WAS HARDENED. By itself. Pharaoh saw that the magicians were able to do what Aaron did.

AND THE LORD SAID…PHARAOH’S HEART IS STUBBORN. Kaved (is stubborn) is a verb in the perfect. It is like the word zaken (was old) in when Isaac was old (Gen. 27:1), chafetz (were pleased) in If the Lord were pleased (Jud. 13:23), ahev (he loveth) in such as he loveth (Gen. 27:9). The mem of me’en (refuseth), which is a root letter, is vocalized with a tzere so that a dagesh is not placed in the alef which follows it. Cheref (jeoparded) in jeoparded their lives (Jud. 5:18) is similar.

GET THEE UNTO PHARAOH IN THE MORNING. It is the custom of the king of Egypt until this very day to go out in the months of Tamuz and Ab to see how high the water has risen. This is the time the river increases. God commanded Moses to go in the morning and stand before the river and perform the sign of the striking of the river in the presence of Pharaoh. He commanded Moses to take and then give to Aaron the rod which he had turned into a serpent before coming unto Pharaoh (Ex. 4:3) and to wave it over the waters of Egypt so that Pharaoh would see with his very eyes the river turn into blood at the moment that Aaron struck it.
AND THOU SHALT SAY UNTO HIM. Say the following to him, because if he does not listen, this is the first plague. The rod which turned into a serpent (v. 10) was not a plague.

THUS SAITH THE LORD. The messenger speaks the word of the one who sent him. Moses was brief, for the term “His messenger” has been omitted. The statement should be understood thus: behold, I His messenger will smite with the rod that is in my hand .
[WITH THE ROD THAT IS IN MY HAND.] Moses said, that is in my hand , even though the rod was in Aaron’s hand because they were equals and both participated in the performance of the sign.
AND THE FISH. Fish is a general term for all things that swarm in the waters.
SHALL LOATHE. Ve-nil’u (shall loathe) is a nifal from the same root as the word la’ah (weary). Its meaning is, will be unable.

AND THE LORD SAID. According to my opinion this is to be understood as follows. Aaron waved his hand and struck the Nile. He also waved his hand toward all the sides of Egypt to turn the waters of all the rivers in the land of Egypt, that is, in the kingdom of Egypt, into blood. The term the waters of Egypt is a general term. Over their rivers is one of its particulars. The term ye’or (stream) refers exclusively to the Nile. There are other rivers in Egypt, for the blood was over all of their country.
OVER THEIR STREAMS. The plural ye’orehem (their streams) is employed because the Nile is found in many places.
THEIR POOLS. Pools of rainwater that form by themselves.

AND OVER THEIR PONDS OF WATER. This refers to fountains, wells, and cisterns. Saadiah Gaon says that the word meyeme (water of), which is the word me (water of) doubled, refers to sweet water while the word me refers to bitter water, as in me ha-yam (waters of the sea). Scripture therefore reads, ha-kore le-me ha-yam (that calleth for the waters of the sea) (Amos 5:8). Now the Gaon forgot that Scripture states, me ha-yarden yikkaretun (the waters of the Jordan shall be cut off) (Josh. 3:13). The word me is always doubled when connected to a pronoun, as in the word memai (my water) (I Sam. 25:11) and in memekha (thy water) (Ezek. 12:18). This mode comes exclusively in the plural form, as it is incorrect to say memi (my water) and memah (her water). We find me used in the singular in because the water of (me) sprinkling was not dashed (Num. 19:13).
[BOTH IN VESSELS OF WOOD AND IN VESSELS OF STONE.] That is, in water found in the homes in vessels made out of wood or basins made out of stone.
AND MOSES AND AARON DID. Scripture notes the smiting of the Nile. However, it does not bother to mention the waving of the hand over all the waters of Egypt.

AND THE MAGICIANS OF EGYPT DID IN LIKE MANNER WITH THEIR SECRET ARTS. The word be-latehem (with their secret arts) comes from the same root as ba-lat (stealthily) in she approached him stealthily (Jud. 4:21). It means with secret things hidden from the eye. A heh has not been omitted from the word, for the heh is not an implied letter in the middle of a word. One may ask: If all the water in Egypt was turned into blood by Aaron, where did the magicians find the water to turn into blood? The answer is: Aaron turned only water that is found above ground into blood. He did not transform any water that was below ground. The magicians dug and brought forth water from beneath the ground and openly turned it into blood. Now, there is a great difference between what Aaron did and what the magicians brought about. Aaron transformed all of the Nile that was before him plus all the water that was in all the borders of Egypt, which he did not see. Furthermore, he changed water that was not standing still but was continually running, with other water taking its place, into blood. Additionally, the plague lasted for seven days. The magicians, on the other hand, were only able to transform a little water standing in a vessel, for a moment, until Pharaoh returned to his house.
AND PHARAOH TURNED. Scripture states even this because it first mentioned the sign of the rod which turned into a serpent and swallowed the other rods.

DIGGED. Many say that the water was as red as blood in the hands of an Egyptian and became clear in the hands of an Israelite. If this is so then why doesn’t the Torah record this sign? I believe that the plagues of blood, frogs, and gnats included both Egyptians and Hebrews, for we shall follow Scripture. These three plagues caused little harm. However, God differentiated between the Egyptians and the Israelites with regard to the swarms, which was a very harmful plague. So too with regard to the plagues of murrain and hail because of their flocks. This was not the case with the boils and locusts, for they left Egypt. Now as the Egyptians digged , so did the Hebrews dig.
WERE FULFILLED. Scripture notes this because unlike the other plagues, this plague lasted many days.
AND THE LORD SPOKE…GO IN UNTO PHARAOH. With your brother Aaron and inform him of the second plague if he does not let my people go.

AND IF. The word ma’en (refuse) is a transitive participle. It is like the word ve-shabbe’ach (wherefore I praised) in Wherefore I praised the dead (Eccles. 4:2). The meaning of nogef (smite) is destroy. It is thus written, And frogs, which destroyed them (Ps. 78:45). The commentaries are divided as to the meaning of the word tzefarde’im (frogs). Many say that it is a type of fish called al-timsach in Arabic that is found in Egypt, that arises from the river and preys upon people. Others say that it is the well-known sound-producing creature which is found in the majority of rivers. This interpretation appears to me to be correct.
AND THE RIVER SHALL SWARM. Ve-sharatz (shall swarm) is a transitive verb. It is like yishretzu (swarm) in Let the waters swarm (Gen. 1:20).
[WHICH SHALL GO UP.] The reason Scripture states this is that the river is always lower than the city.

BOTH UPON THEE, AND UPON THY PEOPLE. Yefet says that Scripture reads, both upon thee, and upon thy people to hint that the frogs shall affect only Pharaoh and his people but not Israel. However, this is no proof. Since Scripture mentions that the frogs shall go up upon him and upon all of his people, there was no reason to mention Israel.

AND THE LORD SAID…STRETCH FORTH THY HAND. Towards the four corners of heaven and the frogs will arise from the canals, from the rivers, and from the pools. However, they will not arise from all gatherings of water.

AND AARON STRETCHED OUT HIS HAND. Behold, Aaron merely stretched forth his hand but did not strike the water as he did the first time. He merely indicated that the frogs could arise from the moment that he stretched out his hand.

AND THE MAGICIANS DID IN LIKE MANNER. In the little water. Pharaoh therefore saw that there was a difference between what Aaron did and what his magicians were able to do. He called Moses because he saw that his magicians could add to the plague but were unable to mitigate it.

THEN PHARAOH CALLED. Pharaoh employed the plural form for entreat ( hatiru ) out of respect for Moses and Aaron. This plague was worse than the first one, for we read, He sent among them…frogs, which destroyed them (Ps. 78:45).
AND MOSES SAID UNTO PHARAOH: HAVE THOU THIS GLORY OVER ME. I will glorify you by entreating the Lord that He take away the plague on a day that you yourself shall designate.
[AND REMAIN IN THE RIVER ONLY.] The reason for mentioning the river is that this is where the frogs started from. Once Scripture notes the river there is no need to mention the canals and pools.

AND HE SAID: AGAINST TOMORROW. Rabbi Samuel ben Hofni says that people usually pray that a plague be removed from them immediately. Pharaoh, however, thought that the plague of frogs resulted from an unpropitious conjunction of heavenly bodies which Moses knew about. He thought that the time for the removal of the frogs had now come. Therefore Pharaoh tested Moses by asking him to extend the plague and said, Against tomorrow .

AND THE FROGS SHALL DEPART. Ve-saru (shall depart) is ultimately accented, contrary to the rules of grammar. We find the same irregularity in the word samu (they put) in that they should put me into the dungeon (Gen. 40:15).

AND MOSES AND AARON WENT OUT. Moses cried unto the Lord because he trusted that the Lord would not put him to shame. Out of his own accord and without the permission of God, he had told Pharaoh, Be it according to thy word .
AND THE LORD DID ACCORDING TO THE WORD OF MOSES. Which he had spoken of his own accord.
AND THEY GATHERED. Va-yitzberu (and they gathered) is similar in meaning to the word va-yitzbor (laid up) in And Joseph laid up corn (Gen. 41:49).
HEAPS. Chomarim chomarim (heaps) is similar in meaning to chamor chamoratayim (heaps upon heaps) (Jud. 15:16).
BUT WHEN PHARAOH SAW THAT THERE WAS RESPITE. The word harevachah (respite) is similar in meaning to ve-ravach (relief) in so Saul found relief (Jud. 16:23).
HE HARDENED HIS HEART. Scripture employs an infinitive ( hakhbed ) in place of a perfect.

AND THE LORD SAID. Note that the first three plagues and signs which Aaron brought about pertained to the lowest elements, as I have explained previously, since two were related to water and one to the dust of the earth. However, the plagues brought about by Moses with his rod related to a higher element. This was so because Moses was on a higher plane than Aaron. Thus the hail and the locusts were brought by the wind, and the darkness was in the air. Moses also brought about the plague of boils. However, three plagues came about without the use of the rod, namely, the swarms of beasts, murrain, and the death of the first-born. One plague, that of the boils, was brought about by Moses with Aaron’s minor participation and without the use of the rod.

[THAT IT MAY BECOME GNATS THROUGHOUT ALL THE LAND OF EGYPT.] This is similar in meaning to And it shall become small dust over all the land of Egypt (Ex. 9:9). The dust which Aaron struck gave birth, as it were, to gnats which went up over all the land of Egypt.

AND THEY DID SO. And they did refers to Moses and Aaron. Moses is included because he told Aaron to smite the dust with the rod. Our verse is similar to and thy rod, wherewith thou smotest the river, take in thy hand (Ex. 17:5).

AND THERE WERE GNATS. Kinnam (gnats) is a generic name. The mem of kinnam is either superfluous or in place of a heh . In any case, it is not a root letter. The mem sometimes serves as the sign of the feminine plural, as in the word tzefardi’im (frogs). This term is a feminine, for when referring to the singular Scripture reads, va-ta’al ha-tzefarde’a (and the frog came up) (Ex. 8:2). The term kinnim is proof of the aforementioned. According to this interpretation the word ha-kinnam is irregular because of its superfluous mem . It is similar to the word rekam (empty) and chinnam (gratuitous). However, Yefet says that the mem of kinnam is a pronominal suffix relating to the Egyptians. He claims that the singular of kinnim (gnats) is kan , in the same way that the singular of pittim (morsels) is pat (morsel). He also says that the word ha-kinnam is similar to the word ha-oholi (my tent) (Josh. 7:21). Do not be amazed that Scripture records that after one spot was struck, all the dust of the earth became gnats throughout all the land of Egypt . Its meaning is that the plague then started. The same is true regarding the plagues of the water and the boils.
AND THE MAGICIANS DID SO. They struck the dust of the earth.
TO BRING FORTH GNATS. To cause the earth to bring forth gnats as Aaron did. However, they could not do so.
[AND THERE WERE GNATS UPON MAN, AND UPON BEAST.] Scripture notes this a second time because the plague was also upon the magicians.

THEN THE MAGICIANS SAID. When the magicians saw that unlike the changing of the rod into a serpent and the plague of blood and frogs where they were able to duplicate Aaron’s actions they were now unable to imitate what Aaron had done, they said to Pharaoh that this plague did not come to liberate Israel but was a disaster sent by God in keeping with the arrangements of the stars dealing with Egypt’s fortune. I have previously explained that Pharaoh did not deny the existence of a Creator. He only denied the existence of the God which Moses revealed to him. Our verse is explained by, it is not His hand that smote us; it was a chance that happened to us (I Sam. 6:9) from heaven. Hence Pharaoh’s heart was hardened. Our interpretation is supported by the fact that the magicians said, This is the finger of God , and not, this is the finger of the Lord, meaning the God of Israel, as Pharaoh did when he exclaimed, Entreat the Lord , with regard to the plague of frogs and then similarly used this term for God in the latter plagues. Furthermore, Moses told Pharaoh that the Nile would be stricken before it was actually plagued, and he likewise informed him that the land would be inundated by frogs before they appeared. However, Moses did not inform Pharaoh that a plague of gnats was about to strike.
AND THE LORD SAID. It is the custom of kings to go out to the river in the morning, for it is good for the eyes to see water.
I WILL SEND. The word mashli’ach (I will send) is in the hifil . It is irregular.
[SWARMS OF FLIES.] The word arov (swarms of flies) refers to a mixture of evil beasts such as lions, wolves, bears, and leopards.
[AND ALSO THE GROUND.] Uninhabited places.

AND I WILL SET APART. Some say that the word ve-hifleti (and I will set apart) is missing an alef . However, I believe that it comes from a root ending in a heh . The meaning of ve-hifleti is, and I will set apart. It is logical to assume that Pharaoh now started to lighten Israel’s burden. When he saw that the Lord put a division between Israel and Egypt he feared to harm them. He now saw the need to send them to offer sacrifices to the Lord, lest he fall upon us with pestilence (Ex. 5:3). Don’t you see that he now gave them permission to sacrifice to the Lord in the land of Egypt?

[THAT I AM THE LORD IN THE MIDST OF THE EARTH.] This is a metaphor. It is the manner of kings to establish their residences in the middle of their kingdoms so as to be equidistant to their borders. The Lord similarly placed the heart, which is “king” over man’s body, in the center of the human corporeal frame. Man’s spirit too is located in the center of the body, as it is written, And (the Lord) formed the spirit of man in the midst of him (Zech. 12:1). There are many proofs from nature that this is so. Scripture states, Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God hath shined forth (Ps. 50:2) because Zion is in the center of the inhabited world and God’s presence is seen in the inhabited world.
AND I WILL PUT A DIVISION. The meaning of pedut is a division. The word pidyon (redemption) is always similar in meaning.
AND THE LORD DID SO. On the morrow, as Moses had spoken.
[AND THERE CAME GRIEVOUS SWARMS.] By themselves. This plague was worse than any of the previous plagues.
AND PHARAOH CALLED. It was now clear to Pharaoh that the plagues came because the children of Israel did not offer sacrifices unto the Lord.
[IN THE LAND.] In his kingdom and not in any other place.

AND MOSES SAID. Rabbi Joshua says that the clause the abomination of the Egyptians was written to disparage idol worship. What Moses actually said to Pharaoh was, “the god of the Egyptians.” Rabbi Joshua further states that the god of Egypt was shaped like a lamb because the Egyptians believed that the constellation of the lamb ruled over their land. It is because of this that the Egyptians did not eat meat. However, if the reason for the Egyptians not eating meat was their worship of the lamb why did they also abstain from ox and goat meat? I believe that the ancient Egyptians in the time of Moses had the same belief currently held by the people of India, who make up more than half of the world. All of them are descendants of Ham. They do not eat meat until this very day. These people also do not drink milk or blood or eat fish or eggs. In other words, they do not eat anything coming from a living creature. Furthermore, they abhor any person who eats any of the aforementioned. They consider shepherding to be an especially disgusting type of work. It is similarly written, for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians (Gen. 47:34). They also do not allow any meat-eating person in their country. If any of them goes to a foreign country he will flee from any place where flesh is eaten. They will not eat anything which a meat-eater has handled. They consider his very garments unclean. It is thus written, because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews (Gen. 43:32). Behold, Potiphar placed everything with the exception of the food which he ate under the care of Joseph, who was then living in his house. Potiphar would not permit him to touch his food because Joseph was a Hebrew. There is no reason to ask, “If this is so, then why did the Egyptians keep cattle?” We find the same to be the case in contemporary India. Horses, asses, and camels were used to carry burdens and for riding. Cattle served to pull the plow and sheep were kept for their wool. I will yet speak on this when I discuss the Passover observed in Egypt. Yefet says that an interrogative heh is missing in the phrase ve-lo yiskelunu , for its meaning is, will they not stone us. However, I believe that the word hen (lo) in hen nizbach (lo, we sacrifice) has the same meaning as the interrogative heh. The meaning of our verse thus is: if we sacrifice ( hen nizbach ) the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, will they not stone us? The word hen in hen hayetah ka-zot (if there hath been such a thing) (Jer. 2:10) is identical.
WE WILL GO THREE DAYS’ JOURNEY INTO THE WILDERNESS. We must remove ourselves from the Egyptians.
[AS HE SHALL COMMAND US.] Regarding the type and number of animals to be selected as sacrificial victims.

AND PHARAOH SAID. The phrase entreat for me should have been placed at the beginning of the verse, as the verse means entreat for me that this plague will be removed and I will let you go to sacrifice in the wilderness as you asked. However, this is on the condition that you go no further than three days’ journey into the desert.

AND MOSES SAID…ONLY LET NOT PHARAOH DEAL DECEITFULLY. The word hetel (deal deceitfully) is irregular. A dagesh should have been placed in the tav , for its heh is a root letter. It should have been vocalized like the word dabber (speak) in behold, I cannot speak (Jer. 1:6). We find the same irregularity in hatel tehatellu vo (mock, will ye mock him) (Job 13:9). The correct vocalization of this word is found in the clause va-yehattel ba-hem eliyahu (that Elijah mocked them) (I Kings 18:27). Moses said, only let not Pharaoh deal deceitfully any more , because he had promised to let the people go during the plague of the frogs and then didn’t.

AND MOSES WENT OUT. There are words in Hebrew that have the same meaning in the kal and hifil. These words come in two forms with one meaning. Examples are: va-yetar (and entreated) in and entreated the Lord and ve-hatarti (and I will entreat) in and I will entreat the Lord (v. 25). Similarly moreh (shoot) and yarah (shot) in which I shoot and he shot an arrow (I Sam. 20:36). However, such words are rare.

AND THE LORD DID. The word va-yasar (and he removed) is grammatically irregular. Roots having a vav as their middle letter are vocalized with a kamatz beneath their first stem letter, i.e., va-yashav (and he returned) and va-yakam (and he got up). However, in cases where the last letter of the root cannot receive a dagesh , i.e., if it is a chet, ayin , or resh , then the first root letter is vocalized with a pattach , as in va-yanach (and rested) in and rested on the seventh day (Ex. 20:11); va-yana (was moved) in and his heart was moved (Is. 7:2); va-yasar (and he turned) in And he turned in unto her (Jud. 4:18). All of the aforementioned applies to words in the kal , because in the hifil roots having a vav as their middle letter are vocalized with a segol beneath their first stem letters in cases where their roots do not end in the letters mentioned above. An example of the aforementioned is va-yashev (and he brought back) in And he brought back all the goods (Gen. 14:16). Now and he removed is written va-yasar rather than va-yaser . It is like va-yasar (and he took off) in And he took off their chariot wheels (Ex. 14:25). However, it appears that va-yasar is a kal and that va-yasar he-arov (and He removed the swarms of flies) means: and the swarms of flies departed.
AND PHARAOH HARDENED HIS HEART. He hardened his heart as he did at the plague of the frogs wherein it is written: he hardened his heart (v. 11).

GO IN UNTO PHARAOH. To his palace. Rabbi Judah Ha-Levi says that two plagues were in the water: one, that it turned red and the fish died; two, that frogs arose from it. Two plagues were on the earth: one of gnats and the second the swarms, which were an assortment of wild animals. And it is written, Let the earth bring forth the living creature (Gen. 1:24). There were likewise two plagues in the air. Murrain is nothing but a change from the normal in the air’s heat or cold. This change causes an untold number to die in an instant, as the spirit of life which resides in the heart depends on the air. The second plague was the boils. Scripture refers to the firmament which is above their heads as the heaven. The seventh plague was a mixture of the sphere of the whirlwind and the sphere of fire. It is thus written, and fire flashing up amidst the hail (v. 24). The eighth was the plague of locusts which the wind brought from afar. The ninth was a wonderful plague in that the light from the two great luminaries and the stars was absent from above the land of Egypt. The tenth was the descent of the destroyer from the spheres of the glory to kill the first-born.
AND WILL HOLD THEM STILL. The word hand or something similar has been omitted. One that holdeth a dog by the ears (Prov. 26:17) is similar.

BEHOLD, THE HAND OF THE LORD IS UPON. Observe, we find that a yod interchanges with a vav , as elsewhere we read, and thou wouldest be (hoveh) their king (Neh. 6:6). The opposite is the case with the vav of kovai (that wait for me) in For they shall not be ashamed that wait for Me (Is. 49:23) which interchanges with a yod in the word ve-kove (but they that wait) in But they that wait for the Lord shall renew their strength (Is. 40:31).

The word dever (murrain) is a collective noun. Its verbal form is found employed only once, in va-tedabber (she destroyed) in she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah (II Chron. 22:10). The book of Kings reads, va-te’abed (and she destroyed) (II Kings 11:1). This interpretation is far-fetched. However, we know of no better one.

AND THE LORD SHALL MAKE A DIVISION…NOTHING. The word davar (nothing) is used in reference to many words joined together, as in ha-davar (the word) in The word that the Lord spoke to Jeremiah (Jer. 46:13). It is also used in reference to a thing, as in our verse. Davar in thou hast not lacked a thing is similar (Deut. 2:7).
AND THE LORD APPOINTED. He set a fixed time for the sign to begin.

AND THE LORD DID. The meaning of and all (kol) the cattle of Egypt died is, that most of the cattle of Egypt died. For behold, it is written, Now therefore send, hasten in thy cattle (v. 19). We find the same with regard to the plague of hail. Scripture reads, and the hail smote every herb of the field (v. 25). The plague of locusts concerning which it is written, and they shall eat the residue of that which is escaped, which remaineth unto you from the hail (Ex. 10:5) is proof of this.

SO MUCH AS ONE. Ad echad means, as I will explain in the song of Moses, so much as one . The meaning of our verse is: even though Pharaoh sent agents and saw that God loves Israel and on their account smote his flocks, he was not so bothered by the death of the flocks during this plague as to let Israel go. Perhaps the plague did not last a long time.
AND IT SHALL BECOME. This was miraculous, that this small amount of soot turned into dust all over the land of Egypt. This plague did not separate out the Israelites.

BLAINS. The alef of avabu’ot (blains) is superfluous, as avabu’ot comes from the same root as tiveh (to boil) in And the fire causeth the waters to boil (Is. 64:1). The word is doubled like the words teshasha’u (shall be dandled) (Is. 66:12) and tesagsegi (thou didst make it to grow) (Is. 17:11).

AND THEY TOOK THE SOOT OF THE FURNACE. Each as earlier noted took handfuls of soot and Moses threw all of it heavenward. It is possible that the magicians were not smitten with the plague of frogs and swarms. Through their wisdom and their knowledge of natural law they searched for a way to gain a small respite. However, their knowledge now failed them, as Scripture tells us. Pharaoh did not ask Moses and Aaron to entreat the Lord because the plague did not last long. We cannot conclude from the plain meaning of the text that since the first plague lasted for seven days all the other plagues did so too. Additionally, we shall pursue the text of Scripture. It is known that the plague of murrain lasted for one hour and the plague of darkness for three days. There is no way to ascertain in which month Moses came and the plagues commenced. However, if our holy sages received this via tradition we accept and abide by it.
AND THE LORD HARDENED THE HEART OF PHARAOH. He therefore did not request Moses to entreat the Lord.
AND THE LORD SAID. Scripture does not here note that Pharaoh went out unto the water. Perhaps he had another reason for rising early.

FOR. Scripture reads, all My plagues because thunder, hail, rain, and fire combined in this plague. We do not find Pharaoh to be as afraid of all the passing plagues as he was of this one. He also said, the Lord is righteous (v. 27).
[THAT THERE IS NONE LIKE ME IN ALL THE EARTH.] This was said in accordance with Egyptian belief that their gods had the power to harm or to benefit.

AND SMITTEN. Va-akh (and smitten) is missing a nun . It is like the word ve-at (though I was offering) in Though I was offering them food (Hos. 11:4). They are both the same. Their roots are nun, tet, heh and nun, kaf, heh .

[PESTILENCE.] Scripture reads, ba-dever (with pestilence) because it refers to the well-known pestilence. It means: I would have killed all of you along with your cattle with the pestilence with which I smote them.

BUT IN VERY DEED FOR THIS CAUSE HAVE I MADE THEE TO STAND. Scripture goes on to explain the meaning of zot (this). It means to show thee My power . And out of the midst thereof as the color of electrum, out of the midst of the fire (Ezek. 1:4) is similar. However, Yefet says that its meaning is, for this plague, the reference being to the plague of hail.

[AND THAT MY NAME MAY BE DECLARED THROUGHOUT ALL THE EARTH.] This does not refer to Pharaoh. On the contrary, the word sapper (be declared) is an infinitive like the word kabbed (promote) in for I will promote thee unto very great honor (Num. 22:17). Its meaning is not that Pharaoh will go all over the world to declare God’s glory, but rather that God’s name would be declared from generation to generation because of the signs which He performed.

AS YET EXALTEST THOU THYSELF AGAINST MY PEOPLE. Mistolel (exaltest) means praises. It comes from the same root as the word salseleha (extol her) in Extol her, and she will exalt thee (Prov. 4:8). Now even though its first root letter is doubled it still belongs among the double roots. It is similar to the word solu (extol) in Extol him that rideth upon the skies (Ps. 68:5). Likewise ve-gilgaltikha (and roll thee down) (Jer. 51:25) is similar to mitgolel (wallowing) (II Sam. 20:12) and golu (roll). However, Rabbi Merinus says that the meaning of mistolel (exaltest) is strengthens and comes from the same root as mesillot in And the king made of the sandalwood pillars (mesillot) for the house of the Lord (II Chron. 9:11). Elsewhere it is written, And the king made of the sandalwood pillars (misad) for the house of the Lord (I Kings 10:12).

I WILL CAUSE IT TO RAIN. It is well known that even today neither rain nor hail comes down upon the land of Egypt. There is no need to explain why this is so. The same is still true of many other places. It was because of this that the Egyptians were greatly afraid, for with the exception of something resembling dew, nothing rains down there.
SEND HASTEN. The word ha-ez (hasten) means make to flee or gather. He-izu (flee) in The inhabitants of Gebim flee to cover (Is. 10:31) is similar.
HE THAT FEARED…MADE FLEE. On that very day.

AND HE THAT REGARDED NOT. There is a meaning in Arabic for the vav of va-ya’azov (left). However, it is not in our power to translate it into another language. Va-yissa (lifted up his eyes) in, On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes (Gen. 22:4) is similar. There are many other similar instances.

AND THE LORD SAID. From a strictly logical point of view it appears that the stretching forth of his hand was with his rod. Behold, it is written afterwards, And Moses stretched forth his rod toward heaven , that is, in the air above. In the open firmament of heaven (Gen. 1:20) is similar.
AND FIRE RAN DOWN. Va-tihalakh (ran down) is a kal form. It expresses going.
UNTO THE EARTH. Contrary to its nature, which is to go up.
AND FIRE FLASHING UP AMIDST THE HAIL. A miracle within a miracle.

AND THE HAIL SMOTE. This was a very strong plague, for it killed man and beast and broke every tree of the field. However, God pitied them and their cattle. Moses did not mention this to Pharaoh because he saw that Pharaoh sent agents and learned that there was not even one of the cattle of the Israelites dead, and yet did not take this to heart.
AND CALLED. Pharaoh said, I have sinned, because he was greatly afraid that he, as was told to him, would be destroyed by the pestilence.

ENTREAT THE LORD. Pharaoh made mention of the glorious name and referred to kolot Elohim (noises from God) because he, as I have already noted, admitted to the existence of a Deity. Moses combined the proper and adjectival names and said, “the Lord God” ( YHVH / Adonai Elohim ) because Pharaoh did not employ the term kolot YHVH / Adonai . The meaning of YHVH / Adonai Elohim is: the Lord alone is God. We never find Moses employing this phrase in the entire Torah. The term Adonai Elohim in O Lord God, Thou hast begun (Deut. 3:24) does not refute the aforementioned, as Adonai is written there with an alef, dalet .
AND MOSES SAID UNTO HIM: AS SOON AS I AM GONE OUT OF THE CITY. The commentaries say that Moses was unable to spread forth his hands in Egypt because it was filled with idols.
THAT THE EARTH IS THE LORD’S. Not yours.

BUT AS FOR THEE. Rabbi Solomon says that the meaning of terem tire’un (ye will not yet fear) is: you do not fear. He interprets terem yishkavu (but before they lay down) (Gen. 19:4) similarly. However, the meaning of this word is not as he imagined, as the subject always follows. Following terem yishkavu (but before they lay down) Scripture reads, the men of the city, even the men of Sodom, compassed the house round: its meaning is, at the time when they lay down they compassed the house round. The word terem (before) in before they call, I will answer (Is. 65:24) and terem (before) in Yea before the fat was made to smoke (I Sam. 2:15) are similar. The same applies to all times the word terem is used. Thus terem never has the meaning of no. Rabbi Saadiah Gaon of blessed memory connected the whole subject. He explained it as follows. Moses said to Pharaoh, I shall pray for the hail to be removed. However, what it destroyed, it destroyed.

The meaning of And the flax and the barley were smitten is, the flax and barley shall not return and I shall not pray for their recovery. Behold, its meaning is, before you fear God and confess and say the Lord is righteous, the barley and flax shall already be smitten. This vav , as I have noted, is correctly used according to the Arabic. However, in my opinion a word has been omitted, its interpretation being: before I spread my hands you will fear the Lord, viz., you and your servants. Moses was being polite. Its implication is, when the plague is removed you will rebel. Therefore Scripture notes afterwards, and (Pharaoh) hardened his heart, he and his servants . We do not find this in any other place.

AND THE FLAX AND THE BARLEY. Scripture relates what happened. It is clear from the word nukkatah (were smitten) and also from the word nukku (were smitten) (v. 32) that the root of makkeh (smite) is nun, kaf, heh . It is similar to the words shuppu (corrode) and ru’u (unsightliness) in And his bones corrode to unsightliness (Job 33:21).
THEY RIPEN LATE. Afilot (ripen late) is an adjective. The word afel (darkness), as in, darkness, and not light , is close in meaning to it. It means that they were beneath the earth and unseen.

POURED. Nittakh (poured) is used in the same sense as ke-hittukh (as is melted) in As silver is melted in the midst of the furnace (Ezek. 22:22). It is a nifal like the word niggash (drew near) in but Moses drew near unto the thick darkness (Ex. 20:18).
AND WHEN PHARAOH SAW. Scripture now mentions, he sinned yet more , because Pharaoh confessed and said, I have sinned this time (v. 27).
[AND HARDENED HIS HEART, HE AND HIS SERVANTS.] From this, Moses’ words, But as for thee and thy servants (v. 30), become clear.
AND THE HEART OF PHARAOH WAS HARDENED. Though he feared this plague more than the earlier ones.

GO IN UNTO PHARAOH. Go in unto him this time and do not be astonished that he has hardened his heart until now, For I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his servants. God mentioned the heart of his servants because their hearts would mellow with the coming of the plague of the locusts.

[FOR I HAVE HARDENED HIS HEART.] Its meaning is: I have hardened his heart that I might show these My signs in the midst of them. The Spanish scholars differ with regard to the word shiti (I might show). Some say that shiti is similar to binu (consider) (Deut. 32:7), simu (set) (Gen. 43:21), and other such words. The same is the case with yashit (he will put), yasim (he will place), yavin (he will understand), and comparable words in all of their forms. Others hold that shiti is a hifil minus the sign of the form, because they found the words yasum (maketh) and la-sus (rejoice) in who maketh a man dumb (Ex. 4:11) and for the Lord will again rejoice over thee for good, as He rejoiced over thy fathers (Deut. 30:9), all of which are kals . Others say that yasis is similar to yasus (he will rejoice) and shiti to sumi (set). They are all kals . In Ex. 12:9 we find: “Behold, I the writer add to the words of this sage as I heard from his mouth.”

AND THAT THOU MAYEST TELL. God spoke to Moses, who is equivalent to all of Israel. Similarly, that ye may know that I am the Lord means that all Israel shall know the aforementioned. The Torah speaks in human terms when it says, I have wrought , for it pictures God as acting as a human being who arranges events in order to avenge himself upon another.

AND MOSES AND AARON WENT IN. We know that Moses would not come in unto Pharaoh unless Aaron was with him, as Aaron was his spokesman. Scripture here mentions Moses and Aaron because now, unlike any of the other instances of the plagues, they were both returned to and finally expelled from the presence of Pharaoh.
TO HUMBLE. Le’anot (to humble) is a nifal . It comes from the same root as ani (humble).

LOCUSTS. Arbeh (locusts) is the name of a type of locust. Perhaps it is so called because it is more numerous than other kinds of locusts. Scripture states, That which the palmer-worm (gazam) hath left hath the locust (arbeh) eaten (Joel 1:4). Concerning it, Scripture states, My great army which I sent among you (Joel 2:25). If this be the case then the alef of arbeh is superfluous.
AND THEY SHALL COVER. Metaphorically speaking.

THAT ONE SHALL NOT BE ABLE TO SEE. The word ish (a man) has been omitted. Yefet says that many days passed between the plague of hail and the plague of locusts, for Scripture states: which groweth for you out of the field .

SHALL BE FILLED. This word is irregularly used in the Hebrew language. The meaning of u-male’u (shall be filled) is that the houses were full of locusts. However, we also find mile’u (fill) in Fill four jars with water (I Kings 18:34) wherein mile’u is a transitive verb. It is as if it were vocalized with a pattach beneath the mem and a dagesh in the lamed and belonged to the conjugational form that receives a dagesh .

[AND HE TURNED.] Rabbi Joshua says that va-yifen (and he turned) refers to Moses, who paid his respects to the throne by facing the king and walking out backwards. However, Yefet says that Moses finished his duties. So too u-fanita (and thou shalt turn) in and thou shalt turn in the morning (Deut. 16:7). However, what shall Yefet do with the word va-yifen (and he looked) in And he looked this way and that way (Ex. 2:12)? Va-yifen is to be explained as coming from the same root as panim (face). It has the same meaning as va-yar (and he saw). Now Moses left the presence of Pharaoh without his permission. Scripture notes this because Pharaoh asked that Moses and Aaron be brought back. After they were returned Pharaoh, in anger, commanded that they be driven out.
AND PHARAOH’S SERVANTS SAID. The meaning of ha-terem teda (knowest thou not yet) is: do you first want it to become clear to you that Egypt is destroyed.

WERE BROUGHT AGAIN. The word et indicates the thing itself. Now whether one says ha-adam ohavi (the man loves me), in which the yod is a first person pronominal suffix, or he says ha-adam ohev oti (the man loves me), the reference being to my very self, the meaning is one and the same. Therefore, if someone says re’uven harag et shimon (Reuben killed Simeon) he is telling us that Simeon has been slain. However, the same is the case if he says, re’uven harag shimon (Reuben killed Simeon). Ve-rav ya’avod tza’ir (and the elder shall serve the younger) (Gen. 25:23) and asher bara Elohim adam (that God created man) (Deut. 4:32) are similar. Do not think that et indicates the direct object because it is often found to be so used. It is also found before the subject, as in u-va ha-ari ve-et ha-dov (and when there came a lion, or a bear) (I Sam. 17:34) and many other similar cases. Rabbi Judah the grammarian says that Scripture reads, va-yushav (were brought again) rather than va-yushevu (were brought again) because of the word et . However, I believe that Scripture reads, va-yushav because Moses was the most important one. Scripture similarly reads, va-tedabber miriam ve-aharon (And Miriam and Aaron spoke) (Num. 12:1) because Miriam was the main speaker.
FOR WE MUST HOLD A FEAST UNTO THE LORD. All of us are obligated to sacrifice unto the Lord.
SO BE THE LORD WITH YOU. Whom you say is with you.

[SEE YE THAT EVIL IS BEFORE YOUR FACE.] The evil is close to you and is before your face. This meaning is also to be connected to for that is what ye desire (v. 11). Hence it is only right that I so act. At this point Pharaoh surmised that they wanted to flee. Note that our Master Moses did not go so far as to lie and say that Israel would return. He merely said that they would travel a three days’ journey (Ex. 9:23). However, the Egyptians thought that they would return. Hence they let them have what they asked. Moses had another reason for acting in this manner. Had Pharaoh given Israel permission to go and Israel did not return, Pharaoh would not have pursued them. However, God commanded Moses to act in this manner so that Pharaoh would chase after them and drown. Behold, this is clearly stated, that they turn back and encamp before Pi-hahiroth (Ex. 14:2). One should not question the acts of God, as He does everything with wisdom, though it be hidden from the eyes even of wise men. We find a similarity in the account of David, viz., And it shall be, when thou hearest the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry-trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself; for then is the Lord gone out before thee to smite the host of the Philistines (II Sam. 5:24).
NOT SO; GO NOW YE THAT ARE MEN. The word gever (man), unlike the word adam (man), always refers to a man in Scripture.
FOR THAT IS WHAT YE DESIRE. The above-noted evil.

FOR THE LOCUSTS. Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen says that ba-arbeh (for the locusts) indicates that Moses placed a locust on the rod. However, this is incorrect. The correct interpretation of ba-arbeh is: so that the locusts would come.

AN EAST WIND. Kadim (east) is an adjective, since kedemah mizrachah (the east side) is a noun. Kadim is so called because it is the first of the sides because the sun begins to shine there. Hence the west is termed achor (hinder side). Compare, Behold, I go forward (kedem), but He is not there, And backward (achor), but I cannot perceive Him (Job 23:8).
BROUGHT THE LOCUSTS. From its place and deposited them in all the kingdom of Egypt.
WENT UP. Neither after them shall be such was prophetically written.
FOR THEY COVERED THE FACE OF THE WHOLE EARTH. The meaning of so the land was darkened is that the locusts intervened between the sun and the land. The land is always dark.
THEN PHARAOH CALLED FOR MOSES AND AARON IN HASTE. Via his messengers. Pharaoh added, I have sinned, because he drove them away from his presence in disgrace.
NOW THEREFORE FORGIVE, I PRAY THEE. I will explain the term sa na (forgive, I pray thee) in the Torah portion Ki Tissa .

[ONLY THIS ONCE.] Because I will not sin again by rebelling against the Lord. Pharaoh did not promise to free the people because Moses was angry. Moses went out of the city as was his wont and prayed.

AND THE LORD TURNED AN EXCEEDING STRONG WEST WIND. West is termed yam in the holy tongue because the great sea which goes out from Spain and passes by the land of Egypt and goes on to the Land of Israel lies in the west. This sea is not to be identified with the Atlantic Ocean because Israel did not inherit that much territory. The Spanish Sea is called the great sea because it is three hundred Persian miles wide, whereas none of the seas in the Land of Israel such as the Sea of Reeds, the Kineret, and the Salt Sea is even thirty Persian miles wide.
BUT THE LORD HARDENED. This is to be understood à la the words of our sages of blessed memory who said, “The door is opened for one who comes to defile himself.”
AND THE LORD SAID. We may logically assume although it is not so stated that Moses’ staff was in his hand.

EVEN DARKNESS WHICH MAY BE FELT. Yefet says that ve-yamesh (which may be felt) is like ve-yamish (and it shall depart); its meaning is: that the darkness to which they have become accustomed shall depart and another type of darkness, thicker than it, shall come. Others say that ve-yamesh is missing an alef . Now the word emesh in the holy tongue refers to the previous night, like emesh (yesternight) in spoke unto me yesternight (Gen. 31:29). It is the same case with the Arabic ams , as the shin and samekh interchange in most of the words. Now their interpretation makes no sense. I believe that ve-yamesh comes from the same root as yemashesh (gropeth) (Deut. 28:29). One cannot argue that yemashesh comes from a double root because with regard to something very similar Scripture uses the term yemishun (handle) in They have hands but handle not (Ps. 115:7). Ve-yamesh refers to Egypt, Egypt being in the singular, as in so Egypt said I will flee (Ex. 14:25). Now the meaning of ve-yamesh choshekh (even darkness which may be felt) is that the Egyptians will feel the darkness with their hands, for the darkness shall be so thick that neither a candle nor a fire shall give off light. They saw not one another (v. 23) neither by the light of day nor by candlelight is proof of the aforementioned.

AND MOSES STRETCHED FORTH. The Egyptians had no way of knowing that three days passed except through the Israelites, who had light. Now there are times when a thick darkness comes over the Atlantic Ocean during which time it is impossible for a person to distinguish between day and night. The aforementioned occasionally lasts for as long as five days. I myself have been there many times.
NEITHER ROSE ANY FROM HIS PLACE. From his house, as in abide ye every man in his place (Ex. 16:29). For where could they go without light?
AND PHARAOH CALLED. After three days when they saw light.

ONLY LET YOUR FLOCKS AND YOUR HERDS BE STAYED. Pharaoh wanted to know what was in Moses’ mind. He wanted to learn whether Moses planned to escape. Pharaoh said, let your little ones also go with you because Moses had earlier told him, We will go with our young and with our old (v. 9).
THOU MUST ALSO GIVE INTO OUR HAND SACRIFICES AND BURNT-OFFERINGS. You are obligated to give into our hands sacrifices and burnt offerings to be brought on the altar on your behalf.

THERE SHALL NOT A HOOF BE LEFT BEHIND. Of any kind that are among our cattle, as we do not know which kind we are to choose and how many of them we will sacrifice. This is the meaning of we know not with what we must serve .
BUT THE LORD HARDENED PHARAOH’S HEART. In a manner similar to for the Lord thy God hardened his spirit, and made his heart obstinate (Deut. 2:30).
THOU SHALT DIE. You will deserve to be put to death for rebelling against the king.
THOU HAST SPOKEN WELL. Ken (well) here has the same meaning as ken (right) in The daughters of Zelophehad speak right (Num. 27:6).
I WILL SEE THY FACE AGAIN NO MORE. For I will never come to you again.

AND THE LORD SPOKE. The chapter opening with the words, Thus saith the Lord (v. 4) should have been connected to the previous verse. However, the chapter stating, Yet one plague more was inserted between them. The reason for this is that Scripture wanted to teach us when Thus saith the Lord was told to Moses. It was related to Moses while he was yet in Midian, viz., Behold, I will slay thy son, thy first-born (Ex. 4:23). Moses was commanded on Mount Sinai that when the time came for the plague of the first-born to arrive, every man should ask jewels of his neighbor. I have already explained why it is there written, but every woman shall ask of her neighbor (Ex. 3:22) and here it is written, and let them ask every man of his neighbor . Now the meaning of And the Lord said unto Moses: Yet one plague more will I bring is that the Lord had already told this to Moses. There are many such cases in Scripture. God said, he shall surely thrust you out , in keeping with His statement, and by a strong hand shall he drive them out of his land (Ex. 6:1).
SPEAK NOW. I have already explained that the word na means now.
AND THE LORD GAVE. Scripture relates that the Lord kept his promise to Moses: of And I will give this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians (Ex. 3:21).
[MOREOVER THE MAN MOSES.] For many let them have what they asked out of respect for Moses.
AND IN THE SIGHT OF THE PEOPLE. The people of Egypt.

ABOUT MIDNIGHT. Some grammarians say that ka-chatzot (about midnight) is an infinitive. Its meaning is, when it shall be exactly one half of the night. They want to compare ka-chatzot ha-laylah (about midnight) to ba-chatzi ha-laylah (at midnight) in And it came to pass at midnight (Ex. 12:29). Now it is common knowledge that it is beyond the ken of a wise man to ascertain the exact moment of noon without great effort and the use of large copper instruments. It goes without saying that it is much harder to ascertain the more difficult time of midnight. I believe that there is no need for all of this since the meaning of ka-chatzot ha-laylah (about midnight) is, when the first half of the night has passed. The same is the case with ba-chatzi ha-laylah in And it came to pass at midnight (Ex. 12:29). It refers to the remaining half of the night. And it came to pass at midnight (ba-chatzi ha-laylah) (Ruth 3:8) and At midnight (chatzot laylah) I will rise to give thanks to thee (Ps. 119:62) are convincing proof of this.
[WILL I GO OUT.] The reference is to the decree that goes out from the Lord.

THE FIRST-BORN OF PHARAOH THAT SITTETH UPON HIS THRONE. Who is fit to sit upon Pharaoh’s throne after him. Moses mentioned the most honored of all the Egyptians, namely, the son of their lord whom all of them serve and also the meanest of them all, namely, the first-born of the maid-servant, who is himself a slave.

[THAT IS BEHIND THE MILL.] Who grinds. Compare, And he did grind in the prison house (Jud. 16:21). I have already explained that the prophets are not careful in preserving the exact wording but are rather concerned with reproducing meanings. The words hagmi’ini (give me to drink) (Gen. 24:17) and hashkini (give me to drink) (Gen. 29:45); zakhor (remember) (Ex. 20:8) and shamor (observe) (Deut. 5:12); sheker (false) (Ex. 20:13) and shav (false) (Deut. 5:17); lo tachmod (thou shalt not covet) (Ex. 20:14) and ve-lo titavveh (neither shalt thou covet) (Deut. 5:18) have one meaning. I will yet discuss this when I comment on the prayer of Moses (Ex. 32:9). Now, the first-born of the maid-servant means the same as the first-born of the captive (Ex. 12:29). The captive woman is a maid-servant who sleeps in the dungeon at night as prisoners do, as was noted by Joseph when he said, that they should put me into the dungeon (Gen. 40:15).

AND THERE SHALL BE A GREAT CRY. We do not find Scripture elsewhere stating anything like kamohu lo nihyatah ve-khamohu lo tosif (such as there hath been none like it, nor shall be like it anymore). The word al (over) has been omitted from our verse and the clause should be understood literally as follows: such as over it there hath been none like it, nor such over it shall be like it a cry anymore.
Such as like it ( kamohu ) refers to havoc, calamity, death, and the like.

SHALL NOT A DOG WHET HIS TONGUE. To frighten them. None whetted his tongue against any of the children of Israel (Josh. 10:21) is similar. Its meaning is that no dog shall bark at them or bite them. Now no dog shall whet his tongue at them or their cattle here on earth. How much more so when He sends a destroyer from heaven to smite their first-born?
AND ALL THESE THY SERVANTS SHALL COME DOWN UNTO ME…SAYING. On your behalf.

AND ALL THE PEOPLE THAT FOLLOW THEE. Be-raglekha (follow thee) means: who are under your dominion. For I will lead them to the place which I desire. And there went up ten thousand at his feet (be-raglav) (Jud. 4:10) is similar. Moses went out in hot anger because Pharaoh had told him, see my face no more (Ex. 10:28).
AND THE LORD SAID. According to the manner of the Hebrews and the rules of language this is to be rendered: and the Lord had already said. There are many other such instances.

AND MOSES. Even though Moses and Aaron did all these wonders which are mentioned in Scripture, Pharaoh’s heart did not soften and he did not let them go, because God hardened his heart. The chapter opening with the words, And it came to pass at midnight (Ex. 12:29) should by right have followed next so that the plagues would be described in order. However, the chapter dealing with, This is the ordinance of the Passover (chap. 12) was inserted in the middle to inform us how the first-born of Israel were saved when the destroyer came upon Egypt.
